Physical-prefix receiver screening uses a shorter sequence than encoder screening

A separately frozen source-semantics unit reuses the same 16 MiB physical-read prefixes and 4,873 RS-exact records. It pins original glass.pyx, droplet.pyx and utils.pyx, rather than treating the encoder constraints as receiver acceptance. In glass.add_dna the seed is registered before screening; the reconstructed Droplet is made without its RS argument. Its screen therefore sees the four-byte header and 32-byte payload, or 144nt, not the full 152nt RS-protected encoded oligo. This predicate comparison does not execute the original receiver, soliton mapping or peeling.

All 4,873 RS-exact physical records pass the full 152nt GC and homopolymer predicate. On the receiver-style 144nt substring, 4,789 pass and 84 fail GC; none fails the homopolymer predicate. Removing the RS suffix changes the GC denominator and can move a screened full oligo outside the receiver threshold. The two predicate geometries therefore disagree on 84 records. This is a documented implementation distinction, not evidence that it caused an original-author reconstruction failure.

Under the inspected FASTQ-prefix order, 196 records are duplicate seeds. Registering each seed before the predicate leaves 4,595 first-seen seeds that pass the 144nt screen and 82 that fail it. No seed has conflicting payload hashes in this prefix. Those counts are conditional on prefix order, not the original abundance-descending preprocessing order. They are not complete receiver acceptance, original source identity or whole-payload recovery.

Every predicate result and seed-order flag is retained in results/dna_fountain_receiver_screen_audit.json, with pinned source-file hashes and the frozen plan. Prefixes replay the earlier ledger exactly. No new sequencing download, fountain decode or local-codec physical validation was performed. The content-page gate remains uncertified.

Source: https://github.com/TeamErlich/dna-fountain at pinned commit 8ee2777aa5e9e101e5d756f7e2449f6672b66f1f. The original receiver has unpinned Python2/Cython dependencies; this unit reproduces the inspected predicate and ordering semantics in Python3, not that entire environment.
